name: Pacific North Subsurface Countercurrent
scope: Declared northern Tsuchiya Jet studied reach from the 155 W mean-section core to the 110 W mean-section core. Western formation and basin continuation east of 110 W are excluded. The section gates truncate a larger current; interpolating bends are editor-selected, not a measured continuous centerline or particle path.
layer: Subsurface northern Tsuchiya Jet, distinct from upper-ocean NECC and equatorial EUC. Source Table 1 gives local mean peak depths of 220 m at 155 W and 130 m at 110 W; these are local supports, not a uniform depth or full vertical boundaries.
time_convention: Editorial connection of mean hydrographic-section peak locations in Johnson and Moore (1997). Historical source compilation 1967-1996 has uneven sampling; no exact regional observation period, monthly axis or dated route reconstructed.
source_locator: Sections 2-3 and Table 1: north SSCC peaks at 155 W 3.5 N/220 m and 110 W 4.5 N/130 m. Transport integration latitude limits and 700-dbar reference are separately defined; they are not route width or a uniform axis layer.
source_citation: Johnson and Moore (1997), The Pacific Subsurface Countercurrents and an Inertial Model, Journal of Physical Oceanography 27, 2448-2459.
source_license: NOAA-hosted article states not subject to U.S. copyright; published by AMS in 1997. Regional facts paraphrased; source figures and historical CTD fields not packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW adopts rounded Table 1 core neighborhoods at 155 W 3.5 N and 110 W 4.5 N as truncation gates. Intermediate 140 W 3.8 N and 125 W 4.2 N are editor-selected connections, not digitized axis points. The path neither assigns a whole-current origin/termination nor merges northern/southern jets or NEUC.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW northward bend assumption; not a width boundary or seasonal axis.
OSW southward bend assumption; not a width boundary or seasonal axis.

scenario_rule: Three declared shapes crossed with uniform longitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 and independent endpoint-latitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 81 editorial cases, not width bounds, seasonal extrema or confidence intervals.
remaining_gates: Review interpolation against compatible northern Tsuchiya Jet velocity fields; selected section gates are not origins or terminations.
Resolve western formation and eastward turning/merging separately from this studied reach.
Extract month/depth-resolved axes before annual length or width ranges.
Keep NEUC at 130 E and the southern Tsuchiya branches as distinct identities; no transported-volume-to-length or integration-band-to-width conversion.
route_extent_kind: 155 W to 110 W northern Tsuchiya reach

supporting_sources.citation: Johnson et al. (2002), Direct measurements of upper ocean currents and water properties across the tropical Pacific during the 1990s.
supporting_sources.locator: Section 3.1: northern subsurface countercurrent/Tsuchiya name; 140 W around 4 N/200 m; eastward shoaling and mean/synoptic differences.
supporting_sources.role: Later naming and layer context; not an additional dated or uniform-depth route.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 81 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
